subject.title: bug: withAllowedHostname only updates allowedHostnames, not hostnameAllowlist — breaks navigate with non-empty hostnameAllowlist

question: Should the fix stay scoped to browser CDP control-policy plumbing, or should OpenClaw change shared SSRF allowlist semantics so `allowedHostnames` can override a non-empty `hostnameAllowlist`?
rationale: Both possible fixes can make this report pass, but only maintainers should choose whether the shared SSRF contract changes or the browser plugin keeps the exception local to its own control plane.

options.title: Use CDP control policy
options.body: Thread `resolveCdpControlPolicy` into Playwright page-selection/navigate CDP connection paths while leaving shared SSRF and page-navigation policy semantics unchanged.

options.title: Broaden shared SSRF semantics
options.body: Make exact `allowedHostnames` additions override `hostnameAllowlist`, accepting a wider security-contract change that needs broader SSRF review.

options.title: Keep strict current behavior
options.body: Require users who configure `hostnameAllowlist` to also add the local CDP host manually, preserving current semantics but keeping the shipped navigation footgun.

recommendation.title: Use CDP control policy
recommendation.body: Thread `resolveCdpControlPolicy` into Playwright page-selection/navigate CDP connection paths while leaving shared SSRF and page-navigation policy semantics unchanged.

likelyOwner.reason: The adjacent local-CDP control-policy fix and prior close comment on a related browser SSRF issue make this the best available routing signal for the boundary choice.
